messages:
raj: Heads-up — seeing a cluster-wide uptick in NVIDIA Xid errors (13 and 31) on the inference gpu-pool-us-west2 over the last ~6 hours. p95 request failures for the batching service jumped from 0.2% to ~2.3%.

emily: Do we have a correlation to a specific model or batch size?

raj: Preliminary correlation looks like majority are from nodes handling large batched seq-length >=1024 jobs and batch_size >=64 (fp16 quantized models).

sam: Can you paste an example dmesg / kernel log?

raj: Sure — here's one excerpt from host gpu-usw2-178 (recent):

```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13, RTX 8000, GPU:0
[ 1234.567891] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1234.567892] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, CE: 00000000
```
\nraj: nvidia-smi on that host right before the failure showed memory ECC corrected errors ticked up on GPU0: `corrected_ecc_count=42` (was <5 normally).

emily: NVM: driver version on that pool? kernel/drivers mismatch can cause Xid 13.

raj: Driver is 525.116.04, CUDA 11.8, kernel 5.15.0-112. We have a mix of driver minor revisions across the fleet (some nodes on 525.85).

maria: For context: Xid 13 = illegal memory access/soft fault, often tied to ECC flips or thermal/hw. Xid 31 = engine halt/CE. Historically we've seen Xid13 when the GPU has rising corrected ECC before a falloff.

sam: Actionable triage steps: 1) identify hosts with >10 Xid events in last 24h, 2) check ECC corrected counts, 3) pin suspicious jobs away, 4) drain and repro on an isolated host, 5) consider GPU replacement if hw errors persist.

infra-bot: Query result: 46 hosts in gpu-pool-us-west2 reported >=1 Xid in last 6h. Top 4 hosts by Xid count: gpu-usw2-178(18), gpu-usw2-043(15), gpu-usw2-201(12), gpu-usw2-089(11).

emily: I can run a fleet-wide CC report and map to workload labels (model id, batch_size). If most traffic to those hosts is from the long-seq inference route, we can short-circuit.

raj: Quick grep across traces shows 82% of failed requests on those hosts are from `inference/long-seq` route and 74% had batching enabled with batch_size >= 48.

sam: Two immediate mitigations we can try (low-risk):
- Set autoscaler to avoid scheduling long-seq batches on hosts with ECC corrected > 20.
- Reduce max batch_size for long-seq route from 128 -> 32 and monitor error rate.

maria: Longer term: schedule a rolling driver upgrade to the latest 535.x (per vendor notes Xid 13 regressions fixed), and add a daily ECC delta alert that triggers at +20 corrected flips in 24h. Also ensure kernel modules match driver builds.

raj: I've queued a canary: changed route config for two canary nodes to cap batch size at 32 and enabled prefix caching offload. Will watch.

infra-bot: Canary update (10m): gpu-usw2-201 shows no new Xid events after config change. p95 failures for that canary dropped from 1.9% -> 0.15%.

emily: Nice. For hosts that still show persistent Xids after traffic isolation, we should run memtest/reliability stress (nvidia-smi --run-inf --stress or nvml diag) and if ECC keeps rising, mark GPUs for RMA.

sam: Also check PCIe lanes/BIOS versions — we've seen flaky cards on older motherboards where reseting the slot clears falloffs for a while. Add a checklist: BIOS, riser inspection, reseat GPU.

maria: Suggest a short doc for SRE on triage steps for Xid 13/31/48/79 mapping to likely root causes (ECC hw, driver/kernel mismatch, thermal throttling, PCIe resets). I can draft.

raj: TL;DR decisions: 1) Temp mitigate by reducing long-seq max_batch=32 on affected pool, 2) Start fleet driver upgrade plan to 535.*, 3) Add ECC-delta alert threshold +20, 4) Run hardware validation on top 10 noisy hosts and prepare replacement schedule.

emily: I'll own the driver rollout plan and can coordinate with hw ops for RMA list.

sam: I'll update the autoscaler predicates to avoid noisy GPUs and add a flag to mark GPU unhealthy for scheduling when corrected_ecc_delta > 20.

raj: Thanks — will follow up with a short postmortem if we confirm hardware vs software root cause. For now watch the canaries and I'll post logs if any new Xid types pop up (48/79 too). :eyes:

maria: Thanks team — useful thread. :thumbsup:
